### sender valilidation

*  email does not verify sender is genuine
   *  problem for spam
   *  would like to reject "spoofed" messages
*  some grafted-on solutions
   *  Sender Policy Framework (RFC 7208)
   *  DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) signatures (RFC 6376)
   *  Domain-Based Nessage Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance (RFC 9989)

### SPF

*  `foo.com IN TXT "v=spf1 a:foo.com mx:bar.com ip:1.2.3.0/24 ~ip:1.2.0.0/16 -all"`
   *  allow from `foo.com`, bar.com's MX servers, 1.2.3.0/24
   *  "softfail" from 1.2.0.0/16
   *  "fail" all others

### SPF and mailing lists

```
MAIL FROM:<mailing-list@mailinglistsite.com>
RCPT TO:<subscriber@foo.example>
DATA
From: <author@bar.example>
...
.
```

*   What SPF record should be checked?


### DomainKeys Idenitifed Mail signature {.smaller}

```
DKIM-Signature: v=1; a=rsa-sha256; q=dns/txt; d=virginia.edu; s=azout-selector; c=relaxed/relaxed;
 h=from:to:cc:subject:date:message-id:references:content-type:mime-version:reply-to:list-id:list-help:list-subscribe:list-unsubscribe:list-post:list-owner:list-archive;
 bh=vI/QgQAmn/cDF8zzsjO1mOAhmBPVjAnxw04hQqBOrH0=;
 b=...
```
*  `c=relaxes/relaxed`: normalize whitespace in headers, body before verifying signature
*  public key in DNS under `azout-selector._domainkey.virginia.edu` (s, d fields)
*  covers message headers listed in `h` field only
*  `bh=...`: hash of message body
*  `b=...` signature itself

### DMARC (RFC 9989)

```
_dmarc.virginia.edu.    3600    IN      TXT     "v=DMARC1; p=reject; rua=mailto:nw0e7asu@ag.us.dmarcian.com; ruf=mailto:nw0e7asu@fr.us.dmarcian.com; fo=1;"
```

*  used with SPF or DKIM
*  policy for requiring _From_ address to be authenticted
   *  this case, `p=reject`: reject (5xx from SMTP ideally) if not
*  method for reporting violations
*  complications to handle `foo@cs.virginia.edu` sending as `bar@virginia.edu` and vice-versa

### Mail from rewriting

*  mailing lists will usually rewrite `From` headers; possible example:
```
From: Some user <user@company.example>
To: mailing-list@organization.example
```
<hr/>
```
From: Some user via mailing-list <mailing-list-...@organization.example>
To: mailing-list@organization.example
Cc: Some User <user@company.example>
```


### greylisting, blocklists

*  greylisting (RFC 6647)
   *  give temporary errors (451) to new SMTP senders
   *  many spammers won't retry later
*  blocklisting
   *  many (usually IP-based) blocklists example: spamhaus
   *  probably means you can't run a mail server on a "home" ISP

### DNS blocklists {.smaller}

*  looking up 127.0.0.2 (test address) on spamhaus.org (a blocklist provider):

```
dig 2.0.0.127.zen.spamhaus.org

;; ANSWER SECTION:
2.0.0.127.zen.spamhaus.org. 60  IN      A       127.0.0.10
2.0.0.127.zen.spamhaus.org. 60  IN      A       127.0.0.2
2.0.0.127.zen.spamhaus.org. 60  IN      A       127.0.0.4
```
